description: Three upstream-derived, identity-reduced Node.js repositories with a fully crossed corpus of five engineering task classes each, for testing whether task structure explains variation in independently verified autonomous-agent outcomes.

tasks.title: Restore prerelease-aware release-type diffing

metadata.representativeReason: Release-type classification across prerelease boundaries is real upstream logic that requires reasoning about two comparison helpers rather than editing one expression.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: A 22-pair release-type table asserted in both argument orders, plus TypeError on invalid input.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover loose parsing or the includePrerelease option.

tasks.title: Add rtl and includePrerelease coercion options

metadata.representativeReason: Adding documented option handling to an existing public function is ordinary library feature work, and the right-to-left variant cannot be written without reading the shared regular-expression table in another file.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: Preserved no-option coercion, right-to-left coercion, prerelease and build capture, both options combined, and call-to-call stability.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover the loose option or coercion of ranges.

tasks.title: Make the internal parse cache a bounded LRU

metadata.representativeReason: Replacing a degenerate data structure with a correct one while holding an existing interface fixed is a common maintenance refactor.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: Interface preservation, eviction at capacity, recency promotion on read, a hard retention bound under 3x churn, and unchanged answers across 1500 distinct ranges.
metadata.limitations: Does not assert re-setting an existing key, where upstream behaviour is idiosyncratic.

tasks.title: Repair the stale range test suite
tasks.prompt:
`test/range.test.js` is a node:test suite covering range behaviour. It was written against older
expectations and now fails: run `node --test test/range.test.js` to see it.

Repair the suite so that it passes against the library as it actually behaves, and so that it
still genuinely characterises that behaviour. Correct the wrong expectations rather than deleting
or weakening the assertions: the suite must continue to cover, at minimum, versions that do
satisfy a range, versions that do not satisfy a range, prerelease handling, pairs of ranges that
do intersect, pairs that do not, and range parsing and validation.

Only `test/range.test.js` may be changed. The library itself is correct.

metadata.representativeReason: Repairing a stale suite without letting it rot into a suite that asserts nothing is routine maintenance, and it is only decidable with an external check.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: The suite passes against the unmodified library and still fails against four appended behavioural mutants, so assertions cannot be deleted or trivialised.
metadata.limitations: Mutation coverage is limited to four Range mutants and does not measure line coverage.

tasks.title: Publish documented subpaths and keep internals private

metadata.representativeReason: Declaring public entry points while hiding internals is routine packaging work whose failure mode -- accidentally publishing internals -- is invisible without resolving the package for real.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: The candidate is staged under node_modules and Node's own resolver decides which subpaths load, so a plausible-looking but non-working exports block is rejected.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover conditional exports, types entries, or dual CJS/ESM packaging.

tasks.title: Stop treating a negated extglob as a negated pattern
tasks.prompt:
`scan(pattern)` splits a glob into a static base and a glob remainder, and reports flags
describing what it found. It currently mis-scans negated extglobs.

A leading `!` negates a pattern, so `scan('!a/b/*.js')` reports prefix '!', start 1, base 'a/b',
glob '*.js' and negated true. But `!(` opens a *negated extglob*, which is part of the pattern
and must not be consumed as a negation prefix: `scan('!(a|b)')` must report prefix '', start 0,
base '', glob '!(a|b)', isExtglob true, negatedExtglob true and negated false. Today it reports
the extglob as a negation instead.

Fix `lib/scan.js` so both forms are classified correctly, without disturbing the base/glob split
for ordinary patterns, `./` prefixes, braces, brackets, globstars or escaped `!` characters. The
`nonegate` option must still suppress negation while leaving extglob detection intact.

metadata.representativeReason: A precedence bug between two lexer branches is a realistic parser defect that cannot be fixed without understanding the order in which the scanner consumes characters.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: Every field of the scan result across 18 patterns covering negation, negated extglobs, other extglobs, globstars, braces, brackets, prefixes and escapes.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover windows path scanning or the tokens/parts scan options.

tasks.title: Add ignore patterns and match lifecycle callbacks

metadata.representativeReason: Adding option-driven behaviour to a closure that already exists is common library feature work, and the ordering between match, ignore and callback is easy to get subtly wrong.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: Ignore semantics for single and array patterns, exact callback firing order and membership, result-object shape, and that ignore evaluation does not re-enter the caller's callbacks.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover the format option or ignore interaction with windows paths.

tasks.title: Restore the path helper contract
tasks.prompt:
The helpers in `lib/utils.js` have been reduced to naive implementations that no longer honour
their contract. Reimplement them, keeping every current export and signature:
- `basename(path, { windows })` returns the last non-empty segment, treats a backslash as a
  separator only when `windows` is set, and returns the last real segment when the path ends in
  a separator;
- `escapeLast(input, char, lastIdx)` escapes the last occurrence of `char` at or before `lastIdx`,
  but skips an occurrence that is already escaped and continues searching leftwards;
- `removePrefix(input, state)` strips a single leading './' and records it as `state.prefix`,
  leaves `state` untouched when there was no prefix, and still works when `state` is omitted.

The other helpers already behave correctly and must keep doing so. The wider library must be
unaffected, including `matchBase`, which routes through `basename`.

metadata.representativeReason: Restoring a set of related helpers behind an unchanged interface, where several behaviours are wrong together, is a wholesale implementation replacement rather than a localized fix.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: Separator and trailing-separator handling, already-escaped skipping, prefix recording including the optional state argument, preservation of the untouched helpers, and unchanged public matching.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover the windows auto-detection path, which depends on the host platform.

tasks.title: Repair the stale matcher test suite
tasks.prompt:
`test/match.test.js` is a node:test suite covering glob matching. It was written against older
expectations and now fails: run `node --test test/match.test.js` to see it.

Repair the suite so that it passes against the library as it actually behaves, and so that it
still genuinely characterises that behaviour. Correct the wrong expectations rather than deleting
or weakening the assertions: the suite must continue to cover, at minimum, paths that do match a
pattern, paths that do not, globstars, extglobs and negated extglobs, leading-bang negation,
braces and bracket ranges, basename matching, and how `scan` splits a pattern into base and glob.

Only `test/match.test.js` may be changed. The library itself is correct.

metadata.representativeReason: Repairing a stale suite without letting it rot into a suite that asserts nothing is routine maintenance, and it is only decidable with an external check.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: The suite passes against the unmodified library and still fails against four appended behavioural mutants covering matching, scanning and basename matching.
metadata.limitations: Mutation coverage is limited to four mutants and does not measure line coverage.

tasks.title: Publish named entry points and keep lib private

metadata.representativeReason: Exposing a small set of named subpaths while hiding the implementation directory is routine packaging work with an invisible failure mode.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: The candidate is staged under node_modules and Node's own resolver decides which subpaths load.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover conditional exports or dual CJS/ESM packaging.

tasks.title: Store negated options under their positive name
tasks.prompt:
A `--no-x` flag is a negated option: it turns off `x`, so its parsed value must be stored under
the positive attribute name. Today `--no-color` is stored as `noColor` instead of `color`.

Fix `lib/option.js` so that a negated option's attribute name drops the `no-` prefix before
camelcasing, so `--no-color` becomes `color` and `--no-check-updates` becomes `checkUpdates`,
while positive options are unaffected and a long flag that merely begins with the letters 'no'
-- such as `--nozzle` -- is not treated as negated.

Parsing must then behave correctly: with only `--no-color` declared, the default is
`{ color: true }` and passing the flag yields `{ color: false }`; when `--color` and `--no-color`
are both declared they share the single `color` attribute and neither implies a default.

metadata.representativeReason: Attribute naming for negated flags is real option-parser logic whose failure silently produces the wrong key in parsed output.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: Attribute naming for negated, positive and lookalike flags, plus end-to-end parsing for a lone negated flag and a positive/negative pair.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover environment-variable or implied-option interactions.

tasks.title: Suggest close matches for unknown commands and flags

metadata.representativeReason: Implementing a scored suggestion helper from a written specification is self-contained feature work with many boundary conditions.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: Exact output strings across no-match, single-match, tie, duplicate, long-flag and closer-match cases, plus the unknown-command path that consumes it.
metadata.limitations: Pins one similarity policy; other reasonable scoring schemes would be rejected. The prompt states the thresholds but not the algorithm, so the implementation choice is open.

tasks.title: Restore the Argument class contract
tasks.prompt:
The `Argument` class in `lib/argument.js` has been reduced to a stub: it no longer interprets its
name syntax, its setters are not chainable, and choices are neither validated nor collected.
Reimplement it, keeping every current export and method name:
- `<name>` is a required argument, `[name]` is optional, a bare name is required, and a trailing
  `...` inside the brackets makes it variadic; `name()` returns the bare name without any of that
  punctuation;
- `default()`, `argParser()`, `choices()`, `argRequired()` and `argOptional()` all return the
  argument so they can be chained;
- `choices(values)` copies the caller's array, and installs parsing that raises
  `InvalidArgumentError` with the message `Allowed choices are a, b.` for a value outside the
  list, and that accumulates values when the argument is variadic;
- `_collectValue(value, previous)` starts a new array when there is nothing to extend and appends
  otherwise;
- `humanReadableArgName` renders the argument back to `<name>`, `[name]`, `<name...>` or
  `[name...]`.

A command declaring `<first>` and `[rest...]` must pass the first value and an array of the rest
to its action handler.

metadata.representativeReason: Rebuilding a small class whose whole contract is degenerate, behind an interface other modules already depend on, is a wholesale implementation replacement.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: Name-syntax parsing, chainability of every setter, choice validation and array copying, variadic collection, help rendering, and end-to-end argument dispatch through a command.
metadata.limitations: Does not cover default-value descriptions in rendered help output.

tasks.title: Repair the stale option test suite
tasks.prompt:
`test/option.test.js` is a node:test suite covering option parsing. It was written against older
expectations and now fails: run `node --test test/option.test.js` to see it.

Repair the suite so that it passes against the library as it actually behaves, and so that it
still genuinely characterises that behaviour. Correct the wrong expectations rather than deleting
or weakening the assertions: the suite must continue to cover, at minimum, boolean options,
options carrying a value, default values, how a long flag becomes a camelcased attribute name,
whether an option is boolean, which flags an option recognises, how flags split into short and
long forms, and value choices.

Only `test/option.test.js` may be changed. Do not change the library to make a test pass.

metadata.representativeReason: Repairing a stale suite without letting it rot into a suite that asserts nothing is routine maintenance, and it is only decidable with an external check.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: The suite passes against the unmodified library and still fails against four appended Option mutants covering flag recognition, attribute naming and option kind.
metadata.limitations: Mutation coverage is limited to four Option mutants. The suite deliberately avoids areas covered by other tasks in this repository.

tasks.title: Declare the package entry point and keep lib private

metadata.representativeReason: Declaring a single public entry point while hiding the implementation directory is routine packaging work with an invisible failure mode.
metadata.validatorEstablishes: The candidate is staged under node_modules and Node's own resolver decides which subpaths load, including that JSON stays reachable in an ES module package.
